html:
South West Africa was the name of Namibia while South Africa ruled it, from its conquest of the German colony in 1915, under a League of Nations mandate from 1920, until independence in 1990.

South Africa ran it almost as a fifth province, settled white farmers on the best land and brought in apartheid laws, with black homelands planned in the 1960s. Contract labour from the north, especially Ovambo men sent to mines and farms, was hated, and a general strike in 1971 shook the system.

The United Nations ended the mandate in 1966 and the World Court called the occupation illegal in 1971, but South Africa stayed. SWAPO took up arms in the war of independence, which ended with UN-supervised independence.
sum: South West Africa was the name of Namibia while South Africa ruled it, from its conquest of the German colony in 1915, under a League of Nations mandate from 1920, until independence in 1990.
